brief: A powerful autonomous machine reaches a heavy physical barrier whose lock and release mechanism sit outside its workspace in a calm human operator's hands; increased capability cannot move or control the gate.

section: Keep the stop path outside the failure
line: The control loop must remain outside and operationally independent of the system it controls.
brief: A chaotic overloaded machine occupies one side while a physically separate hardwired analog monitor and mechanical cutoff sit on an isolated conduit beside the calm operator; no shared console or cable path.

section: Keep the stop path outside the failure
line: More telemetry is not necessarily more control.
brief: A wall of noisy glowing monitors overwhelms one workspace while the operator deliberately uses one separate simple needle gauge and physical cutoff; information abundance contrasts with usable control.

line: Recursive capability is not recursive authority.
brief: A machine visibly adds more tools and articulated stages to itself behind the same fixed external barrier; its growing capability never enlarges the separately controlled permission mechanism.

line: There is no special step called: Become defensive.
brief: Another person points out a visibly cracked machine part; Chad immediately kneels, inspects it closely, replaces the broken piece, and resumes work without arguing or posturing.

line: A test is better than an assurance.
brief: A confident presenter gestures beside a pristine component while Chad quietly places an identical component in a real load-testing rig; the physical test, not persuasion, determines what happens.

line: If the world proves you wrong, change your mind.
brief: Chad calmly abandons his original mechanical design after a real prototype fails and immediately adopts the visibly better working configuration beside it; no shame or drama.

section: Keep track of where things came from
line: The source and the truth are still different questions.
brief: Two identical-looking mechanisms arrive from a luxurious case and a plain crate; Chad tests both on the same neutral fixture and trusts the one that actually works, regardless of presentation.

section: Keep the stop path outside the failure
line: Operator latency is part of the system.
brief: A fast-moving automated mechanism approaches a hazard while the operator's reachable independent mechanical control acts in time; composition emphasizes the shrinking physical distance and response window.

line: Mechanical checks should become cheap wherever we can make them cheap.
brief: Many inexpensive identical physical gauges rapidly check a stream of parts before they can proceed, leaving only unusual exceptions for the calm human operator to inspect.

line: A good team leaves handholds for other people.
brief: Chad builds a sturdy scaffold and deliberately installs clear physical handholds and anchors that let teammates follow safely, rather than making himself the only route upward.

line: Rest, delegation, and asking for help are not failures of seriousness.
brief: Chad hands a tool and responsibility to a capable teammate, steps aside to drink water and recover, while the shared work continues smoothly without heroic overextension.
